Differential analysis using DAssemble

Source: R/dassemble.R
DAssemble.Rd

The DAssemble function implements an ensemble strategy for differential analysis. Users can select a single core model and optionally augment it with up to three enhancer models. Enhancers are simple, often nonparametric tests that provide complementary evidence. P-values from the core and enhancer models are combined using the Cauchy Combination Test (CCT).

Usage

DAssemble(
  features,
  metadata = NULL,
  core_method = NULL,
  enhancers = NULL,
  expVar = "group",
  coVars = NULL,
  random_effects = NULL,
  method_args = NULL,
  assay_name = NULL,
  p_adj = "BY",
  enhancer_norm = "TSS",
  return_components = TRUE,
  return_subensembles = FALSE
)

Arguments

features

A MultiAssayExperiment object, or a data.frame with samples in rows and features in columns.

metadata

A data.frame with sample metadata. Leave as NULL when features is a MultiAssayExperiment; sample metadata is then taken from colData(features).

core_method

Character scalar naming the core method to run, or NULL / "none" for enhancer-only analysis.

enhancers

Character vector containing any of "WLX", "LR", and "KS".

expVar

Character scalar naming the binary exposure variable in metadata or colData(features).

coVars

Optional character vector naming covariates to include in covariate-aware core methods and logistic-regression enhancers.

random_effects

Optional character vector naming grouping variables for random intercepts in longitudinal-compatible methods.

method_args

Optional named list of method-specific control arguments. Use method_args$core for arguments shared by the selected core method, method_args$enhancer for arguments shared by enhancers, and/or method names such as method_args$Maaslin3 or method_args$LR for method-specific overrides. Matching arguments override DAssemble wrapper defaults before the underlying function is called. For the LR enhancer, the wrapper-specific option method_args$LR$separation_method = "firth" switches the cross-sectional presence/absence logistic fit from the default MaAsLin3-style augmented logistic fit to bias-reduced fitting via brglm2. For the Maaslin2 core, method_args$Maaslin2$median_comparison = TRUE applies the internal median-comparison adjustment to raw fit$results before the exposure-specific result table is standardized.

assay_name

Name of the assay/experiment to use when features is a MultiAssayExperiment. Required when the object contains multiple experiments.

p_adj

Multiple-testing correction method passed to stats::p.adjust.

enhancer_norm

Normalization method for enhancer tests. One of "TSS", "CLR", "TMM", or "SCRAN".

return_components

Logical; if TRUE, return per-method component result tables.

return_subensembles

Logical; if TRUE, return CCT sub-ensemble results for all available method subsets.

Value

A list containing the CCT-ranked joint results in res, the analyzed feature table in features, elapsed time in Time.min, and a named components list when return_components = TRUE. Each component is the standardized result table from one selected core method or enhancer. Optional CCT sub-ensemble results are returned in ensembles.

Examples

features <- data.frame(
  taxon1 = c(12, 9, 11, 8, 25, 21, 23, 26),
  taxon2 = c(30, 28, 31, 29, 10, 12, 11, 9),
  taxon3 = c(5, 6, 4, 7, 5, 4, 6, 5),
  taxon4 = c(8, 7, 9, 6, 12, 13, 11, 14),
  row.names = paste0("sample", seq_len(8))
)
metadata <- data.frame(
  group = factor(rep(c("control", "case"), each = 4)),
  row.names = rownames(features)
)
result <- DAssemble(
  features = features,
  metadata = metadata,
  core_method = NULL,
  enhancers = "LR",
  expVar = "group",
  method_args = list(
    LR = list(control = glm.control(maxit = 50))
  )
)
head(result$res)
#>        feature metadata coef_LR pval_LR pval_joint qval
#> taxon1  taxon1    group      NA      NA         NA   NA
#> taxon2  taxon2    group      NA      NA         NA   NA
#> taxon3  taxon3    group      NA      NA         NA   NA
#> taxon4  taxon4    group      NA      NA         NA   NA
